correctness.rationale: The signed source RESULT.md was read directly from actual Git blob db50dce42f46684dff1e1a0f2f1f205620e0ee2d. All three frequencies are odd, so Q(theta+pi)=-Q(theta), and nonnegativity of 1+Q forces |Q|<=1. Q(0)<=1 and Q(pi/4)<=1 give a+b+c<=1 and (a-b-c)/sqrt(2)<=1, hence 2a<=1+sqrt(2). Equality gives both contacts; derivative at the interior circle point pi/4 gives a+3b-5c=0 and uniquely fixes a,b,c. Independently expanded Chebyshev T1,T3,T5 with SymPy exact radicals and verified 1-Q(x)=(4-2sqrt(2))(1-x)(x-1/sqrt(2))^2[x^2+(1+sqrt(2))x+1+sqrt(2)/2]; the quadratic discriminant is -1. Hence Q(x)<=1 on [-1,1], and oddness gives Q(x)>=-1. This analytic factorization, not the 20,001-point numerical source check, handles every theta; normalization psi(1)=a/2 is correct.
residual_risks: Only continuous real even trigonometric polynomials with exactly allowed higher harmonics 3,5; complex or finite cyclic-grid analogues are not proved.

value.rationale: The normalized first Fourier coefficient of a nonnegative sparse cosine polynomial is a natural sharp positive-definiteness/integer-support invariant. The support {1,3,5} is the lowest genuinely three-odd-frequency case and the two-contact geometry determines a unique algebraic extremizer. Exact value and equality rigidity are independently useful; they are not just a name substitution or a sample grid bound.
residual_risks: Does not settle arbitrary support H, discrete cyclic versions, or complex variants.

final_claim: For real trigonometric polynomials 1+a cos(theta)+b cos(3theta)+c cos(5theta)>=0 for all theta, maximal a=(1+sqrt(2))/2 with unique extremal b=(2-3sqrt(2))/8,c=(2-sqrt(2))/8; the corresponding finitely supported positive-definite sequence has maximal psi(1)=(1+sqrt(2))/4.
limitations: The classification is limited to continuous real even nonnegative trigonometric polynomials with frequencies 1,3,5; finite grid checks alone cannot prove global positivity.
Unindexed cosine-polynomial literature remains a residual originality risk.
